title: Implement ModelBroker trait and stub provider
purpose: Create the only allowed model access boundary for AgentCore while preserving local-only and testable execution.
scope: Define ModelBroker trait for plan, classify, summarize, and sanitize requests.
Define structured request and response types with provider id, model id, digest, latency, confidence, and bounded output.
Implement StubModelProvider that deterministically returns valid structured responses for tests.
Add timeout, cancellation, max-output-size, and fail-closed behavior.
Prevent ModelBroker from receiving raw secret values; only secret handles and redacted summaries are allowed.
Document future provider slots for local model runtime and optional remote model runtime.
acceptance_criteria: AgentCore can plan through StubModelProvider without network access.
Invalid model output is rejected before it becomes a PlanSpec.
Timeouts and provider failures degrade to Suspended or FailedClosed, not tool execution.
ModelBroker calls are logged with metadata but not raw secret values.
No module except ModelBroker directly calls model providers.
verification: Feed malformed provider output and confirm rejection.
Simulate provider timeout and confirm no EffectPrepared event is produced.
Search source for direct provider calls outside ModelBroker.
risk_notes: A weak ModelBroker boundary would let model integrations leak into policy or executor code.
implementation_steps: Define ModelBroker trait for plan, classify, summarize, and sanitize requests.
Define request and response envelopes with provider id, model id, template version, timeout, output bound, confidence, latency, and digest metadata.
Implement deterministic StubModelProvider for offline acceptance and CI tests.
Validate bounded structured output before Planner can consume it.
Handle invalid JSON, oversized output, timeout, cancellation, and provider failure as fail-closed outcomes.
Log only model metadata and reject raw secret values at the broker boundary.
failure_modes: Malformed or oversized provider output reaches Planner as valid structure.
Provider timeout or cancellation advances into tool execution.
Model output containing shell commands becomes a tool call.
Raw secrets are sent to provider context or stored in model call logs.
A module other than ModelBroker directly calls model providers.

verification_matrix.expected: stub, validation, bounded output, timeout, cancellation, and metadata-only logging tests pass
provider usage is contained by ModelBroker or tests

blocked_until: Malformed output is rejected before Planner.
